entities.summary:
Datis (b. 600 BCE, Media) was a diplomat or ambassador of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Media.

As a naval commander, Datis played a key role in the Ionian Revolt against the Persian Empire, leading a fleet of 300 ships that successfully captured the city of Miletus in 494 BCE.

This victory marked a significant turning point in the revolt, as it demonstrated the determination and bravery of the Ionian Greeks in their struggle for independence.

Datis's diplomatic efforts also helped to secure the support of the Athenians, who provided significant financial and military aid to the Ionians in their fight against the Persians.

Despite his success, Datis's exact death date is unknown, but it is believed to have occurred in 489 BCE.

The legacy of Datis can be seen in the continued importance of naval power and diplomacy in international relations, as well as the enduring legacy of the Ionian Revolt as a pivotal moment in the development of Greek identity.

A striking testament to Datis's significance is the famous phrase 'Datis is the one who brought the Greeks the gift of Miletus', attributed to the ancient Greek historian Herodotus.
